literal: If there are those who are wronged and cannot obtain justice themselves, they may go to the envoys to lodge complaints, and the envoys shall investigate.
idiomatic: If any are wronged and cannot obtain justice themselves, they may go to the envoys to lodge complaints, and the envoys shall investigate.

literal: If one is truly pure and capable and praised by all, yet lodges a false complaint to seek justice, reverse the crime upon him.
idiomatic: If one is truly pure and capable and praised by all, yet lodges a false complaint to seek justice, the crime is reversed upon him.

literal: If an envoy accepts bribes and judgment is not fair, they may go to the Imperial Chariot Office to appeal.
idiomatic: If an envoy accepts bribes and judgment is not fair, they may appeal to the Imperial Chariot Office.

literal: Those who are unfilial to parents, disobedient to elders, who as officials are wicked and violent, and who are bandits and thieves—each shall be reported by name.
idiomatic: Those unfilial to parents, disobedient to elders, wicked and violent as officials, and bandits and thieves shall each be reported by name.

literal: Those who conceal them shall be punished with the crime of what they concealed.
idiomatic: Those who conceal them shall be punished with the crime of what they concealed.

literal: " That month the state of Zheyi sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: " That month the state of Zheyi sent envoys with tribute.

literal: Day wuyin: the Emperor hunted at Mount Duni.
idiomatic: On the wuyin day the emperor hunted at Mount Duni.

literal: Day jiashen: returned to the palace.
idiomatic: On the jiashen day he returned to the palace.

literal: Autumn, seventh month, day bingchen: the imperial carriage traveled to Hexi.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on the bingchen day, the emperor went to Hexi.

literal: Eighth month, day dinghai: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the dinghai day, the court returned to the palace.

literal: Winter, tenth month: Persia and the state of Shule each sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter Persia and the state of Shule each sent envoys with tribute.

literal: Day gengwu: Duke of Liaoxi Chang Ying was made Grand Preceptor and advanced to prince.
idiomatic: On the gengwu day Duke of Liaoxi Chang Ying was made Grand Preceptor and advanced to prince.

literal: Second year, spring, first month, day yimao: Empress Feng was installed.
idiomatic: In the first month of spring of the second year, on the yimao day, Empress Feng was installed.

literal: Second month, day dingsi: the imperial son Hong was installed as Crown Prince; a general amnesty throughout the realm.
idiomatic: In the second month, on the dingsi day, the imperial son Hong was installed as Crown Prince and a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.

literal: Several thousand families of Dingling hid in Mount Jingxing and gathered as bandits.
idiomatic: Several thousand families of Dingling hid on Mount Jingxing and gathered as bandits.

literal: An edict ordered Governor of Dingzhou Xu Zongzhi and Governor of Bingzhou Qifo Chenglong to suppress and pacify them.
idiomatic: An edict ordered Governor of Dingzhou Xu Zongzhi and Governor of Bingzhou Qifo Chenglong to suppress and pacify them.

literal: Summer, sixth month: Palace Guard Officer Yu Pan, Yuan Ti, and others plotted treason and were executed.
idiomatic: In the sixth month of summer Palace Guard Officer Yu Pan, Yuan Ti, and others plotted treason and were executed.

literal: Autumn, eighth month, day jiashen: hunted in Hexi.
idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn, on the jiashen day, he hunted in Hexi.

literal: That month General Who Pacifies the West, Duke of Yuyang Juan, attacked Yiwu in the north, took its city, and returned with great booty.
idiomatic: That month Juan, General Who Pacifies the West and Duke of Yuyang, attacked Yiwu in the north, took its city, and returned with great booty.

literal: Ninth month, day xinsi: Duke of Hedong Lu Pi and Duke of Lingling Lu Ge were both advanced to prince.
idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the xinsi day, Duke of Hedong Lu Pi and Duke of Lingling Lu Ge were both advanced to prince.

literal: Winter, tenth month, day jiashen: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on the jiashen day, the court returned to the palace.

literal: Day jiawu: a partial amnesty in the capital.
idiomatic: On the jiawu day there was a partial amnesty in the capital.

literal: Eleventh month: Director of the Secretariat Yuan He of Xiping changed enfeoffment to Prince of Longxi.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month Yuan He, Director of the Secretariat of Xiping, changed enfeoffment to Prince of Longxi.

literal: The states of Yanda and Pulan each sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: The states of Yanda and Pulan each sent envoys with tribute.

literal: Liu Jun's Administrator of Puyang Jiang Longju and Administrator of Xinping Yang Bolun each abandoned their commanderies and led officials and people to surrender.
idiomatic: Liu Jun's Administrator of Puyang Jiang Longju and Administrator of Xinping Yang Bolun each abandoned their commanderies and led officials and people to surrender.

literal: Third year, spring, first month, day renxu: hunted at Mount Guo.
idiomatic: In the first month of spring of the third year, on the renxu day, he hunted at Mount Guo.

literal: Day wuchen: returned to the palace.
idiomatic: On the wuchen day he returned to the palace.

literal: Sogdiana and the state of Khotan each sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: Sogdiana and the state of Khotan each sent envoys with tribute.

literal: Duke of Yuyang Juan was summoned and made Grand Commandant, advanced to prince, and Recorder of Secretariat Affairs.
idiomatic: Juan, Duke of Yuyang, was summoned, made Grand Commandant, advanced to prince, and made Recorder of Secretariat Affairs.

literal: Summer, fifth month, day gengshen: hunted at Mount Song.
idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer, on the gengshen day, he hunted at Mount Song.

literal: Day jisi: returned to the palace.
idiomatic: On the jisi day he returned to the palace.

literal: The imperial younger brother Xincheng was enfeoffed as Prince of Yangping.
idiomatic: The emperor's younger brother Xincheng was enfeoffed as Prince of Yangping.

literal: Sixth month, day guimao: the imperial carriage traveled to Yinshan.
idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the guimao day, the emperor went to Yinshan.

literal: Autumn, eighth month: hunted north of Yinshan.
idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn he hunted north of Yinshan.

literal: Day jihai: returned to the palace.
idiomatic: On the jihai day he returned to the palace.

literal: Winter, tenth month: about to tour east; an edict ordered Grand Preceptor Chang Ying to erect a traveling palace at Huangshan in Liaoxi.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, about to tour east, an edict ordered Grand Preceptor Chang Ying to erect a traveling palace at Huangshan in Liaoxi.

literal: Eleventh month: the barbarian chief Wen Hulong led more than a thousand families to submit inward.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month the barbarian chief Wen Hulong led more than a thousand families to submit.

literal: Twelfth month: because five provinces and garrisons suffered locusts and the people were hungry, envoys were sent to open granaries for relief.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month, because five provinces and garrisons suffered locusts and the people were hungry, envoys were sent to open granaries for relief.

literal: That month Khotan, Buyeo, and more than fifty other states each sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: That month Khotan, Buyeo, and more than fifty other states each sent envoys with tribute.

literal: Fourth year, spring, first month, day bingwu first of month: wine prohibition was first established.
idiomatic: On the first day of the first month of spring of the fourth year, the bingwu day, a wine prohibition was first established.

literal: Day yimao: the imperial carriage traveled to the Guangning Hot Springs Palace, then toured east through Pingzhou.
idiomatic: On the yimao day the emperor went to the Guangning Hot Springs Palace, then toured east through Pingzhou.

literal: Day gengwu: reached Huangshan Palace in Liaoxi; feasted for several days and personally received the aged, inquiring after their hardships.
idiomatic: On the gengwu day he reached Huangshan Palace in Liaoxi, feasted for several days, and personally received the aged, inquiring after their hardships.

literal: Second month, day bingzi: ascended Mount Jieshi, viewed the blue sea, and held a great feast for the assembled ministers at the foot of the mountain; distributions of rewards and advancement in rank, each according to rank.
idiomatic: In the second month, on the bingzi day, he ascended Mount Jieshi, viewed the blue sea, and held a great feast for the assembled ministers at the foot of the mountain; rewards and advancement in rank were distributed according to rank.

literal: Mount Jieshi was renamed Mount Leyou; an altar was built at the seashore to record the journey.
idiomatic: Mount Jieshi was renamed Mount Leyou and an altar was built at the seashore to record the journey.

literal: Day wuyin: traveled south to Xinzhou and hunted at Guangchuan.
idiomatic: On the wuyin day he traveled south to Xinzhou and hunted at Guangchuan.

literal: Third month, day dingwei: viewed horse-shooting at Zhongshan.
idiomatic: In the third month, on the dingwei day, he viewed horse-shooting at Zhongshan.

literal: The commanderies and states passed through were granted one year's exemption from levies.
idiomatic: The commanderies and states he passed through were granted one year's exemption from levies.

literal: Day bingchen: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: On the bingchen day the court returned to the palace.

literal: The Taihua Hall was raised.
idiomatic: The Taihua Hall was raised.

literal: Day yichou: Prince of Dongping Lu Hou died.
idiomatic: On the yichou day Prince of Dongping Lu Hou died.

literal: Summer, fifth month, day renxu: an edict said: "We, from assuming the throne until now, have repeatedly issued edicts of leniency, abolishing what is troublesome and harsh, removing what is not urgent, wishing to let things obtain their place and people settle in their occupations.
idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer, on the renxu day, an edict said, "From assuming the throne until now we have repeatedly issued edicts of leniency, abolishing what is troublesome and harsh and removing what is not urgent, wishing to let things obtain their place and people settle in their occupations.

literal: Yet the hundred-li governors cannot spread the imperial favor; their seeking and desire are insatiable; they cut off official goods for their own use, making tax levies hang in deficit;
idiomatic: Yet the hundred-li governors cannot spread the imperial favor; their greed is insatiable; they seize official goods for themselves, leaving tax levies in deficit;

literal: then with extreme severity they lay the blame on the people.
idiomatic: then with extreme severity they lay the blame on the people.

literal: They seek harshly to escape blame and never change their fear.
idiomatic: They seek harshly to escape blame and never change their ways.

literal: The state's system makes levies and corvée light; in recent years miscellaneous levies have been reduced, yet the provinces and commanderies everywhere have arrears—not because officials in office have failed in guidance and lost their place, or been greedy beyond measure—who made it come to this?
idiomatic: The state's system makes levies and corvée light; in recent years miscellaneous levies have been reduced, yet provinces and commanderies everywhere have arrears. Is it not because officials in office have failed in guidance, or been greedy beyond measure? Who made it come to this?

literal: From now on, if regular levies are not fulfilled and the people do not settle in their occupations, those who govern the people shall additionally receive the death penalty.
idiomatic: From now on, if regular levies are not fulfilled and the people do not settle in their occupations, those who govern the people shall additionally receive the death penalty.

literal: Proclaim throughout the realm to accord with Our intent."
idiomatic: Proclaim throughout the realm to accord with our intent."

literal: " Sixth month, day bingshen: hunted at Mount Song.
idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the bingshen day, he hunted at Mount Song.

literal: Autumn, seventh month, day gengwu: the imperial carriage traveled to Hexi.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on the gengwu day, the emperor went to Hexi.

literal: Ninth month, day yisi: returned to the palace.
idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the yisi day, he returned to the palace.

literal: Day xinhai: the Taihua Hall was completed.
idiomatic: On the xinhai day the Taihua Hall was completed.

literal: Day bingyin: feasted the assembled ministers; a general amnesty throughout the realm.
idiomatic: On the bingyin day he feasted the assembled ministers and proclaimed a general amnesty throughout the realm.

literal: Winter, tenth month, day jiaxu: toured north.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on the jiaxu day, he toured north.

literal: Reaching Yinshan, there was an old tomb destroyed and abandoned; an edict said: "Formerly Ji Wen of Zhou buried dry bones and the realm turned to benevolence.
idiomatic: Reaching Yinshan, there was an old tomb destroyed and abandoned. An edict said, "Formerly King Wen of Zhou buried dry bones and the realm turned to benevolence.

literal: From now on, whoever digs up or destroys tombs and mounds shall be beheaded.
idiomatic: From now on, whoever digs up or destroys tombs and mounds shall be beheaded.

literal: Liu Jun's general Yin Xiaozu was repairing two fortresses east of the Qingshui; an edict ordered General Who Guards the West, Duke of Tianshui Feng Jiaowen, and others to attack him.
idiomatic: Liu Jun's general Yin Xiaozu was repairing two fortresses east of the Qingshui; an edict ordered Feng Jiaowen, General Who Guards the West and Duke of Tianshui, and others to attack him.

literal: Day xinmao: the imperial carriage halted at Mount Chelun; stones were piled to record the journey.
idiomatic: On the xinmao day the court halted at Mount Chelun and piled stones to record the journey.

literal: Eleventh month: an edict ordered General Who Conquers the West Pi Baozi and three other commanders with thirty thousand horsemen to assist in attacking Xiaozu.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month an edict ordered General Who Conquers the West Pi Baozi and three other commanders with thirty thousand horsemen to assist in attacking Xiaozu.

literal: [2] The imperial carriage crossed the desert; the Rouran vanished without trace and fled far away; their separate division Wuzhu Huitui and Kushi Tui led their hosts to surrender.
idiomatic: [2] The court crossed the desert; the Rouran vanished without trace and fled far away; their separate division Wuzhu Huitui and Kushi Tui led their hosts to surrender.

literal: Twelfth month: General Who Conquers the East, Prince of Zhongshan Tuozhen, died.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month Tuozhen, General Who Conquers the East and Prince of Zhongshan, died.

literal: Fifth year, spring, first month, day jisi first of month: General Who Conquers the West Pi Baozi raided as far as Gaoping, greatly defeated Xiaozu, and beheaded and captured more than five thousand.
idiomatic: On the first day of the first month of spring of the fifth year, the jisi day, General Who Conquers the West Pi Baozi raided as far as Gaoping, greatly defeated Xiaozu, and beheaded and captured more than five thousand.

literal: Second month, day jiyou: Palace Attendant, Minister of the Masses, Duke of Henan Yi Ba, died.
idiomatic: In the second month, on the jiyou day, Yi Ba, Palace Attendant, Minister of the Masses, and Duke of Henan, died.

literal: Third month, day gengyin: a partial amnesty in the capital for those below death in punishment.
idiomatic: In the third month, on the gengyin day, there was a partial amnesty in the capital for those below death in punishment.

literal: Summer, fourth month, day yisi: the imperial younger brother's son Tui was enfeoffed as Prince of Jingzhao.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on the yisi day, the emperor's younger brother's son Tui was enfeoffed as Prince of Jingzhao.

literal: Fifth month: the state of Juchang sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: In the fifth month the state of Juchang sent envoys with tribute.

literal: Sixth month, day wushen: the imperial carriage traveled to Yinshan.
idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the wushen day, the emperor went to Yinshan.

literal: Autumn, eighth month, day gengxu: then traveled to Yunzhong.
idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn, on the gengxu day, he then went to Yunzhong.

literal: Day renxu: returned to the palace.
idiomatic: On the renxu day he returned to the palace.

literal: Ninth month, day wuchen: an edict said: "Rewards must be for those with merit; punishments must be examined for those with guilt—this is the same through antiquity and the constant pattern from of old.
idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the wuchen day, an edict said, "Rewards must go to those with merit; punishments must be examined for those with guilt—this is the same through antiquity and the constant pattern from of old.

literal: Governors who face the people and devour the common people to build up their households, so that royal levies are not fulfilled—even when their term is full and they leave office, their prior arrears should be reckoned and their crimes and punishments corrected.
idiomatic: Governors who face the people and devour the common people to build up their households, so that royal levies are not fulfilled—even when their term is full and they leave office, their prior arrears should be reckoned and their crimes corrected.

literal: Yet the responsible officials fail in oversight and do not impeach and correct, letting the guilty roam free in ease and the guiltless wrongly suffer their wrong—this opens the road of wickedness and depravity and lengthens the heart of greed and violence. Is this what is called weighing circumstances in imposing punishment to correct the realm?
idiomatic: Yet the responsible officials fail in oversight and do not impeach and correct, letting the guilty roam free and the guiltless wrongly suffer—this opens the road of wickedness and lengthens greed and violence. Is this what is called weighing circumstances in imposing punishment to correct the realm?

literal: From now on, for all who transfer and replace office, they shall list their performance ratings while in office and, according to regulations, impose punishment.
idiomatic: From now on, for all who transfer and leave office, they shall list their performance ratings while in office and, according to regulations, impose punishment.

literal: Those who achieve merit shall receive added rank and favor; those with faults shall be exposed to punishment and execution, so that ability and inability are clearly distinguished and punishment and reward do not err.
idiomatic: Those who achieve merit shall receive added rank and favor; those with faults shall be exposed to punishment, so that ability and inability are clearly distinguished and punishment and reward do not err.

literal: The responsible officials shall clearly make regulations and take them as a constant model."
idiomatic: The responsible officials shall clearly make regulations and take them as a constant model."

literal: Three-Director Equipage, Duke of Dunhuang Li Bao, died.
idiomatic: Li Bao, Three-Director Equipage and Duke of Dunhuang, died.

literal: Winter, twelfth month, day wushen: an edict said: "We have received the great enterprise and rule the host; We think to restore government and teaching to succor the myriad people.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month of winter, on the wushen day, an edict said, "We have received the great enterprise and rule the host; we think to restore government and teaching to succor the myriad people.

literal: Therefore We lighten levies and collections to fill their wealth and lighten corvée to ease their strength, wishing to let the common people cultivate their occupations so that people are not in want.
idiomatic: Therefore we lighten levies and collections to fill their wealth and lighten corvée to ease their strength, wishing to let the common people cultivate their occupations so that none are in want.

literal: Yet the Six Garrisons, Yunzhong, Gaoping, the Two Yongs, and Qinzhou everywhere met disaster and drought, and the year's grain was not harvested.
idiomatic: Yet the Six Garrisons, Yunzhong, Gaoping, the Two Yongs, and Qinzhou everywhere met disaster and drought, and the year's grain was not harvested.

literal: Let granaries and storehouses be opened to relieve them.
idiomatic: Let granaries and storehouses be opened to relieve them.

literal: Those who have fled and wandered, instruct them to return to their native places.
idiomatic: Those who have fled and wandered, instruct them to return to their native places.

literal: Those who wish to buy grain in other regions—make the neighboring commanderies at the passes open the roads of trade.
idiomatic: Those who wish to buy grain in other regions—make the neighboring commanderies at the passes open the roads of trade.

literal: If the officials in charge do not divide duties evenly, so that the sovereign's favor does not reach below and the people below are not provided for in their time, add the heavy penalty—there shall be no escape."
idiomatic: If the officials in charge do not divide duties evenly, so that the sovereign's favor does not reach below and the people below are not provided for in their time, add the heavy penalty—there shall be no escape."

literal: First year of Heping, spring, first month, day jiazi first of month: a general amnesty; the era name was changed.
idiomatic: On the first day of the first month of spring of the first year of Heping, the jiazi day, there was a general amnesty and the era name was changed.

literal: [3] Day gengwu: an edict ordered Palace Attendant Feng Kan as envoy to Liu Jun.
idiomatic: [3] On the gengwu day an edict ordered Palace Attendant Feng Kan as envoy to Liu Jun.

literal: Second month: General of the Guard, Prince of Le'an Liang, supervised the armies of East Yong, Tujing, and Liubi west toward Hexi; General Who Conquers the West Pi Baozi and others supervised the Hexi armies south toward Shilou, to attack the rebel Hu of Hexi.
idiomatic: In the second month General of the Guard Liang, Prince of Le'an, supervised the armies of East Yong, Tujing, and Liubi west toward Hexi; Pi Baozi, General Who Conquers the West, and others supervised the Hexi armies south toward Shilou to attack the rebel Hu of Hexi.

literal: Summer, fourth month, day wuxu: Empress Dowager Chang died at Shou'an Palace.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on the wuxu day, Empress Dowager Chang died at Shou'an Palace.

literal: Fifth month, day guiyou: Empress Dowager Zhao was buried at Mingji Mountain in Guangning.
idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the guiyou day, Empress Dowager Zhao was buried at Mingji Mountain in Guangning.

literal: Sixth month, day jiawu: an edict ordered General Who Conquers the West, Prince of Yangping Xincheng, and others to supervise the armies of Tongwan and Gaoping and march by the southern route; Duke of Nanjun Li Hui and others to supervise the Liangzhou armies and march by the northern route, to attack Murong Shiyin of Tuyuhun.
idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the jiawu day, an edict ordered Xincheng, General Who Conquers the West and Prince of Yangping, and others to supervise the armies of Tongwan and Gaoping and march by the southern route; Li Hui, Duke of Nanjun, and others to supervise the Liangzhou armies and march by the northern route to attack Murong Shiyin of Tuyuhun.

literal: When Cui Hao was executed the historiographical office was abolished; at this time it was restored.
idiomatic: When Cui Hao was executed the historiographical office was abolished; at this time it was restored.

literal: The rebel Hu of Hexi came to Chang'an to confess guilt; envoys were sent to comfort them.
idiomatic: The rebel Hu of Hexi came to Chang'an to confess guilt; envoys were sent to comfort them.
